note: test_sdcard starts Process_SDCard and returns at once; the process writes and reads back 100 sectors per loop, forever, until 'kill test_sdcard' raises its kill request. It writes raw sectors from sector 0 upward, so it destroys the partition table and file system of the card in the slot.

tests.note: with no test running, the clean function only raises a kill request that the next launch clears; kill is on ukos-serial's unsafe list

then.await: (?s)^Card type             sdcard V\.[12]$.*^Card size \[Bytes\]     [1-9][0-9]*$.*^Read  time for 100 sectors: +[0-9]+-us, sector nb +0$.*^Read  time for 100 sectors: +[0-9]+-us, sector nb +100$

tests.note: OVERWRITES the first sectors of the card: pass --have sdcard-scratch only with a card whose contents you do not need. Two write/read/compare rounds (sectors 0-99 and 100-199), then kill; the process must leave the list and release the sdcard reservation (checked by health-after). A missing or unreadable card prints 'Error: status = ...' and logs a fatal record, which also fails health-after
